A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Direct Coverage Optimization study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments on MATH, Mathlib, and MiniF2F, including coverage, confidence distributions, theorem-proving success, and expert-iteration results.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original results for Llama-3-70B, AIME24, difficulty-dependent training effects, and empirical calibration checks.

M1.justification: The DCO loss, confidence-dependent gradient factor, sample filtering, step-wise theorem-proving variant, ensemble strategy, and approximate CoT variant are retained. The added experiments and explanations do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds AIME24 evaluation of models trained on MATH, introducing an out-of-distribution mathematical question-answering scenario. Existing MATH, Mathlib, and MiniF2F coverage remains; the larger model and difficulty analyses do not independently add task coverage.

E2.justification: CE remains the experimental comparator, including in the new larger-model and AIME24 comparisons. Existing theorem-proving comparisons are retained. Newly discussed methods such as BonBon, BOND, and entropic distribution matching are cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with Llama-3-70B experiments, difficulty-stratified gradient diagnostics at 11% and 86% of the first epoch, and calibration testing using beam width 256 and the top 16 completions or answers. Existing experiments retain their stated splits, training budgets, and testing procedures.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether easy examples harm coverage late in training and whether DCO preferentially attenuates their gradients (Section 4.4; Figures 2 and 15). Appendix C.6 tests the approximate-calibration assumption. Larger-model and AIME24 checks also examine whether the overconfidence findings persist beyond the original direct-answer setting.

E5.justification: Figures 2 and 15 add error bars for difficulty-conditioned diagnostic estimates, and Figure 2 specifies averaging over batches. The new error bars are not defined. Table 3 retains its standard-error reporting, and no additional training-run or seed counts are documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results while retaining Tables 1–3 and moving v1 Table 4 unchanged to Table 6. New Tables 4 and 5 report CE pass@4k declining across epochs from 84.2% to 65.9% for Llama-3-70B on MATH and from 80.5% to 35.8% on AIME24. New plots report DCO coverage, difficulty effects, and calibration findings; these are additional settings and analyses, not improvements over replaced v1 scores.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 defines a batch-gradient directional-derivative diagnostic for negative log-coverage test loss and explains its sign as indicating beneficial or harmful training influence. The original coverage theory, confidence-bound lemmas, and Appendix A proofs are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the same central claims: CE can misalign training with pass@N, overconfidence explains this failure, and DCO improves alignment by limiting confidence. The new evidence supports these claims without redefining their core scope.

C2.justification: v2 refines the overconfidence explanation by identifying continued training on easy examples as harmful and interpreting DCO as suppressing their contribution. Appendix B adds a substantive qualification about CoT training overhead and the tradeoff between Monte Carlo precision and computation.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds H200/B200 hardware information for larger models and discloses computational assumptions and estimates for approximate DCO: approximately 50 petaflops for online generation versus 5 for a forward-backward pass, with about 30% GPU-memory overhead. Existing hyperparameters, implementation instructions, and the code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands positioning relative to best-of-N distillation, entropy-based fine-tuning, catastrophic forgetting, and small-data fine-tuning, adding works including BonBon, BOND, LIMA, and LIMO. The primary positioning around alignment between training and test-time strategies remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 revises related-work prose, adds Section 4.4, and expands Appendices B and C with explanatory subsections and cross-references. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained; the revision is primarily targeted expansion rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial display groups for difficulty effects, calibration, larger-model results, and AIME24, including new tables and multi-panel figures. Existing displays are retained and relocated or renumbered. Figure 8 redisplays the existing coverage analysis with N'=256 highlighted, and the retained CoT histogram receives revised axis ticks.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical basis of the central explanation. Unlike v1, it directly checks the calibration assumption, investigates difficulty-dependent training effects, and tests the direct-answer findings with a 70B model and an out-of-distribution dataset. These additions address important gaps in mechanism validation and generality. The new computational-cost disclosure also makes the CoT variant's practical tradeoffs clearer. Although the new error bars remain undefined, the stronger validation and transparency provide a substantial overall gain.
